arxiv-2006-03520.description: Abstract The demonstration of quantum speedup, also known as quantum computational supremacy, that is the ability of quantum computers to outperform dramatically their classical counterparts, is an important milestone in the field of quantum computing. arxiv-2208-13222.title: Rapid decline in the lightcurves of luminous supernovae by jet-driven bipolar explosions
arxiv-2208-13222.creator: Muhammad Akashi, Amir Michaelis, Noam Soker
arxiv-2208-13222.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Akashi, Amir Michaelis, Noam Soker. We calculate the lightcurves of jet-driven bipolar core collapse supernova (CCSN) explosions into a bipolar circumstellar mater (CSM) and show that an equatorial observer finds the lightcurves to possess a rapid, and even an abrupt, drop. The scenario that might lead to such an explosion morphology is a common envelope evolution (CEE) where shortly before the CCSN explosion the red supergiant progenitor interacts with a more compact companion that spirals-in and spins-up the core.

arxiv-2311-15883.description: Abstract Concurrent multi-player mean-payoff games are important models for systems of agents with individual, non-dichotomous preferences. arxiv-2312-12474.title: Principled Weight Initialisation for Input-Convex Neural Networks
arxiv-2312-12474.creator: Pieter-Jan Hoedt & Günter Klambauer
arxiv-2312-12474.description: Abstract icnn are networks that guarantee convexity in their input-output mapping. These networks have been successfully applied for energy-based modelling, optimal transport problems and learning invariances. The convexity of icnn is achieved by using non-decreasing convex activation functions and non-negative weights. Because of these peculiarities, previous initialisation strategies, which implicitly assume centred weights, are not effective for icnn .

pmc-13030682.title: Closed vs. Open-Skill Contexts in Basketball: Insights into Reactive and Nonreactive Short Distance Sprint Performance More Closely Aligned with Game Demands
pmc-13030682.creator: Asaf Shalom, Roni Gottlieb, Julio Calleja-Gonzalez
pmc-13030682.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Basketball requires frequent short-distance sprints performed under both predictable (closed-skill) and unpredictable (open-skill) conditions. Objectives: This study compared sprint performance between closed- and open-skill conditions in 37 professional male basketball players aged 16–18 years. We aimed to determine whether sprint times differ between conditions and distances, test for a condition-by-distance interaction, and evaluate whether player rankings remain consistent across conditions. Methods: All players completed 5 m and 10 m sprints under both closed- and open-skill formats.

pmc-13051117.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:In China, improved cancer survival contrasts with persistent pessimistic attitudes among clinicians, which impacts care quality. We developed a “Whole-Process Management” (WPM) training program to bridge this gap by reshaping internal medicine residents’ understanding of the cancer care continuum.Objective:To investigate whether a WPM clinical training strategy can transform pessimistic attitudes toward cancer care and foster a more integrated understanding of palliative therapy among internal medicine residents.Design:A pre-post study utilizing semi-structured interviews.
